strategy_objective_guidance:
- The evaluator scores only valid packings through

Execution must finish before the subprocess timeout, normally about 350 seconds.
- The reported sum is not scored and is not required to match the calculated sum; it only produces a warning when inconsistent. Nevertheless, report `np.sum(radii)` to avoid needless diagnostics. Runtime, symmetry, visual quality, method elegance, and proximity to the reference construction are not rewarded.
- Validity is near its maximum only when the construction is robustly feasible: one overlap or boundary violation collapses the entire score to zero. Once validity is secured, the largest remaining lever is the total radius sum. The target ratio can exceed 1; `2.635` is not a cap, so the highest-scoring program is simply the valid construction with the largest evaluator-computed sum, not necessarily one that merely reaches the reference.

This directly targets the scored sum and can refine unequal radii and boundary contacts.
- **Global stochastic search followed by feasibility polishing:** use `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution` over bounded center/radius variables with a penalty for boundary violations and pair overlaps, then pass the best candidate to `scipy.optimize.minimize` (`'SLSQP'` or `'trust-constr'`). strategies.title: [stripwise-radius-transfer] Two-row subsystem replacement

strategies.title: [triangular-defect-topology] Defected triangular-lattice exploration

strategies.plan:

strategies.title: [disk-cluster-swap] Discrete four-cluster exchange search
strategies.plan:

The falsifiable threshold is `2.63600`; success requires that the cluster exchange produce a sum above this value. strategies.plan:

The falsifiable threshold is a feasible sum above \(2.63700\). The new degree of freedom is a non-layered contact topology generated by sequential empty-space growth; the incumbent’s row parameterization cannot reach such a topology regardless of SLSQP tolerances.

This should remain below roughly 20 seconds because each subproblem has at most 12 center variables and all radius variables are fixed.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent only optimizes adjacent two-row blocks and can leave a row globally misregistered when a boundary circle is radius-limited by a distant diagonal neighbor. The corridor objective is the global LP sum, so a move is accepted only when it benefits all 26 circles rather than merely the active band.

strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: boundary-weighted-coordinate-blocks

Replacement scope: Replace the incumbent’s six two-row SLSQP subsystems and the subsequent four-stage joint continuation with an alternating weighted block-coordinate phase. Retain the existing row seeds and fixed-center radius LP.

Compute budget: At most 4 row allocations × 3 sweeps × 4 blocks, with at most 70 SLSQP iterations per block; perform one LP after every accepted block. This should remain below roughly 20 seconds because each block contains only 8–12 circles and the LP has 26 variables.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent optimizes a selected pair of rows but gives every circle equal objective weight and then freezes the geometry during the final continuation stages. Partition each layout into four overlapping blocks: the bottom two rows, top two rows, left half of all rows, and right half of all rows. In each block, optimize centers and radii jointly while all other circles remain fixed, but use objective weights 1.25 for circles whose current nearest boundary is a square edge and 1.0 otherwise. This preferentially enlarges the boundary-limited disks instead of allowing the LP to spend nearly all available slack on interior disks. After each successful block, solve the global radius LP, so previously improved boundary disks can transfer slack to their neighbors. Use all 325 pair constraints and four boundary constraints per circle in every block, and reject any result with minimum slack below \(10^{-7}\). The new overlapping vertical/horizontal decomposition can move a boundary disk and its diagonal neighbors together, a degree of freedom not available in the incumbent’s strictly adjacent-row decomposition.

Expected-gain check: the new blocks explicitly optimize boundary-limited disks together with their orthogonal and diagonal neighbors; accept only candidates exceeding the incumbent’s \(2.6359830322\) sum, with a falsifiable target of at least \(2.6362\) while retaining a complete feasible incumbent fallback.

strategies.title: [corridor-width-enumeration] Enumerated unequal-width corridor topology
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: corridor-width-enumeration

Replacement scope: Replace the initial five-row seed generation and all local polishing with a mesoscopic enumeration of corridor populations. Keep the global fixed-center radius LP and one final feasibility polish.

Compute budget: Enumerate exactly the 10 ordered population patterns obtained by permuting \((6,6,5,5,4)\) and retaining the lexicographically first representative under vertical reflection. For each pattern, run one 110-iteration SLSQP solve over all centers with radii held at the LP solution, then one 130-iteration joint solve over centers and radii. This is 10 starts and 2 optimizer calls per start; expected runtime is 25–60 seconds.

Gain mechanism: Use five horizontal corridors with populations \((6,6,5,5,4)\), rather than forcing four 5-circle corridors plus one 6-circle corridor. Place each corridor’s disks at equally spaced normalized abscissae, but initialize its vertical position from the available corridor width and alternate the phase of the 6-, 5-, and 4-circle corridors. The two 6-circle corridors create dense horizontal bands; the 4-circle corridor creates a deliberately wide band containing larger disks. Optimize every center independently under the full pairwise constraints, while adding a small deterministic quadratic penalty only to deviations from the initial corridor order to prevent row crossing. Remove that penalty in the joint solve. This topology creates a large-radius central corridor and lets the surrounding 5/6-circle bands absorb the resulting unequal vertical gaps, which cannot occur in the incumbent’s fixed \(6,5,5,5,5\) row topology.

For every candidate, recompute radii with the exact linear program \(r_i+r_j\le d_{ij}\), \(r_i\le x_i,1-x_i,y_i,1-y_i\), then shrink by \(2\times10^{-7}\). Retain the best independently validated candidate and preserve the incumbent if none is better.

Expected-gain check: the 4-circle corridor introduces four positions with substantially larger horizontal clearance and removes the incumbent’s mandatory five-circle occupancy in that band; the evaluator test is a valid sum above \(2.6365\), otherwise the incumbent fallback must be returned.

strategies.title: [contact-graph-randomized-growth] Deterministic randomized contact-graph growth
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: contact-graph-randomized-growth

Replacement scope: Replace the complete fixed row-layout construction with a deterministic multistart sequential growth construction followed by one global nonlinear polish. Do not use the incumbent’s row allocations as seeds.

Compute budget: Use exactly 12 deterministic seeds. For each seed, insert 26 circles one at a time into a \(5\times5\) triangular-lattice scaffold with one of twelve prescribed vacancy locations and one of three prescribed insertion orders. At each insertion, perform at most 18 candidate-position evaluations. Then run one global SLSQP solve for at most 180 iterations, followed by a radius LP. Expected runtime is 30–90 seconds.

Gain mechanism: Maintain a growing contact graph rather than a row graph. Begin with four corner-adjacent disks and repeatedly insert the next disk at the feasible intersection of two or three existing offset circles, using offsets equal to the current LP radii plus a deterministic \(0.004\) exploratory inflation. Candidate intersections are scored by the sum of distances to the nearest four existing centers, with a deterministic tie-break toward the square center. The 12 seeds vary the vacancy in the triangular scaffold and whether growth proceeds from the boundary, center, or alternating boundary-center order. After every four insertions, solve the fixed-center radius LP and use those radii for the next offset construction. The final joint SLSQP has all centers and radii free, so it can remove insertion artifacts and create unequal-radius contacts. This permits non-row contact graphs with T-junctions and a single intentional defect, whereas every incumbent seed starts from parallel rows and its local optimizers generally preserve that graph.

Reject any candidate having a boundary or pair slack below \(3\times10^{-7}\), and shrink accepted radii by \(10^{-7}\). Keep the incumbent as a valid fallback.

Expected-gain check: the insertion graph can produce a non-row defect and locally larger void-filling disks that the incumbent’s row seeds cannot reach without a topology change; the falsifiable threshold is a validated sum above \(2.6370\), with invalid or lower candidates discarded.
